Optional Shader Controls

MelonUI.Shaders contains OpenGLShaderElement and ShaderDisplay. These are optional graphics controls and are not required for the normal console UI library.

OpenGLShaderElement

OpenGLShaderElement renders a GLSL shader. Constructing or compiling the control does not create a graphics context. Call Init on the application main thread before awaiting the UI loop:

C# Example

MXML Example

After compiling the MXML, use page.Find<OpenGLShaderElement>("Shader")!.Init() before awaiting RunAsync. ShaderSource can supply the GLSL directly instead of a file. Shader file loading is separate from MXML includes; provide a host path that can be read. ErrorMessage describes initialization or rendering failures.

Actual output depends on the shader, GPU and driver. The repository shader demo includes a complete shader and startup/resize checks.

ShaderDisplay

ShaderDisplay uses Windows/Direct3D compute. It allocates its resources when needed and displays its built-in gradient unless you supply another shader:

C# Example

MXML Example

UpdateShader<T> takes a factory receiving ReadWriteTexture2D<float4>. T must be a struct implementing IComputeShader and IComputeShaderDescriptor<T>. Check ErrorMessage when the device or shader cannot run.

Lifetime and Testing

Workers publish complete frames together with their dimensions. During resizing, the previous completed frame is clipped using its own size. Detach pauses reusable graphics activity, while final disposal joins workers and releases native resources.
